notice: All diagnostic recommendations and triage steps are generated by the NetFusion Diagnostic Rule Engine for NOC offline triage. Direct command dispatch is disabled until a live SSH/gRPC backend bridge is configured.

br-remote-rtr01.name: br-remote-rtr01
br-remote-rtr01.issueTitle: WAN Interface Saturation & Physical Layer CRC Corruption
br-remote-rtr01.probableRootCause: Duplex/speed mismatch or physical degradation on the broadband fiber converter uplink (GigabitEthernet0/0/1), combined with unshaped bulk backup traffic exceeding the 1Gbps CIR.
anomalies: 1,482 input CRC errors and 3,410 buffer dropouts

diagnosticSteps.title: Validate Interface Counters & Error Deltas
diagnosticSteps.action: Inspect interface operational status and check whether CRC errors are continuing to increment in real-time.
diagnosticSteps.expectedResult: Full-duplex, 1000Mb/s, 0 incrementing CRC errors after reset. If errors increment rapidly, suspect cable or SFP.

diagnosticSteps.title: Inspect Top Talkers via NetFlow / IP SLA
diagnosticSteps.action: Determine which hosts or traffic classes are monopolizing the upstream queue.
diagnosticSteps.sampleCommand: show ip cache flow | sort 4 | head 10
diagnosticSteps.expectedResult: Verify if unexpected offsite backup sync or unthrottled media streaming is consuming link headroom.

diagnosticSteps.title: Check QoS Policy Drop Statistics
diagnosticSteps.action: Confirm whether the class-default queue is tail-dropping priority business traffic.
diagnosticSteps.expectedResult: Voice/Control plane traffic should show 0 drops; Bulk-Data class should enforce policing.

diagnosticSteps.title: Engage ISP Telecom Provider
diagnosticSteps.action: If optical levels (DOM) are normal (-14 dBm to -3 dBm) and cable has been verified, open Ticket with ISP circuit ID #CKT-WEST-9104.
diagnosticSteps.sampleCommand: show controllers GigabitEthernet0/0/1 phy | include (Tx Power|Rx Power)
diagnosticSteps.expectedResult: Confirm upstream CIR and verify ISP edge switch port configuration.

hq-edge-rtr02.name: hq-edge-rtr02
hq-edge-rtr02.issueTitle: IPsec Crypto Engine High Utilization & CPU Interrupt Strain
hq-edge-rtr02.probableRootCause: Sustained crypto hardware queue backlog during automated IPsec Security Association (SA) re-key cycle with AWS Virtual Private Gateway, aggravated by fragmented jumbo packets traversing a 1400-byte MTU tunnel.
anomalies: Total CPU load at 88.6% (Crypto interrupt process: 42%)

diagnosticSteps.title: Inspect Active IPsec Security Associations
diagnosticSteps.action: Verify phase 1 (ISAKMP) and phase 2 (IPsec) status, SPI sequence numbers, and lifetime timers.
diagnosticSteps.expectedResult: Status: UP-ACTIVE. Verify no rapid re-key flapping or duplicate SAs.

diagnosticSteps.title: Check CPU Process Breakdown
diagnosticSteps.action: Isolate high-cycle consumers between control-plane BGP, IPsec crypto daemon, and packet forwarding.
diagnosticSteps.expectedResult: Identify if 'Crypto SW Pk' or 'IP Input' is commanding >40% CPU cycles.

diagnosticSteps.title: Validate MSS Clamping & DF-Bit Handling
diagnosticSteps.action: Ensure TCP Maximum Segment Size (MSS) clamping is configured to 1360 bytes to prevent router-level packet fragmentation.
diagnosticSteps.sampleCommand: show run interface Tunnel0 | include ip tcp adjust-mss
diagnosticSteps.expectedResult: 'ip tcp adjust-mss 1360' must be enabled on the tunnel interface.

aws-ec2-worker-01.name: aws-ec2-worker-01
aws-ec2-worker-01.probableRootCause: Celery asynchronous queue worker experiencing high task volume from batch telemetry indexing, consuming 78.4% CPU on an 8-vCPU c5.2xlarge instance.
anomalies: Task backlog: 1,840 pending jobs in Redis queue

diagnosticSteps.title: Inspect Worker Concurrency & Celery Process Tree
diagnosticSteps.action: Check process table on the worker node to see if long-running tasks are blocking the event loop.
diagnosticSteps.sampleCommand: ps aux --sort=-%cpu | head -10; celery -A app status
diagnosticSteps.expectedResult: Confirm all worker subprocesses are alive and not blocked on external database locks.

diagnosticSteps.title: Evaluate Auto Scaling Group (ASG) Scale-Out Trigger
diagnosticSteps.action: Verify CloudWatch alarm metric 'CPUUtilization > 75% for 2 consecutive periods' trigger status.
diagnosticSteps.expectedResult: Ensure desired capacity can safely scale from 2 to 3 instances in us-east-1a/b.

aws-rds-postgres-primary.name: aws-rds-postgres-primary
aws-rds-postgres-primary.probableRootCause: No active issues detected. Database is operating well within nominal performance parameters (CPU: 36.2%, Connections: 142/500, IOPS: 3,420).
anomalies: Zero replication lag to read-replica (18ms roundtrip sync)

diagnosticSteps.title: Inspect Active Connection Pool & Long-Running Queries
diagnosticSteps.action: Query pg_stat_activity to monitor slow query duration.
diagnosticSteps.sampleCommand: SELECT pid, now() - query_start AS duration, query, state FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state != 'idle' ORDER BY duration DESC LIMIT 5;

diagnosticSteps.title: Review Multi-AZ Replication Health
diagnosticSteps.action: Confirm synchronous commit state between Primary (AZ-A) and Standby (AZ-B).

hq-core-rtr01.name: hq-core-rtr01
hq-core-rtr01.probableRootCause: System operating smoothly. Direct Connect 10G link is carrying 6.42 Gbps ingress / 7.80 Gbps egress without packet drops or BGP instability.
anomalies: BGP neighbors 4/4 Established with AWS Transit Gateway

diagnosticSteps.title: Verify BGP Route Summary & Prefix Count
diagnosticSteps.action: Check BGP peer stability to confirm no route flapping across Direct Connect.
diagnosticSteps.expectedResult: All peer states Established; Prefix count matching expected 14 routes.

diagnosticSteps.title: Inspect Hardware Forwarding Plane & TCAM Utilization
diagnosticSteps.action: Verify Ternary Content-Addressable Memory (TCAM) table headroom for FIB entries.
diagnosticSteps.sampleCommand: show platform hardware qfp active infrastructure fib summary
